slice.subject: modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk rmcp-v3.1.4 Streamable HTTP trusted-principal middleware seam
source_findings: StreamableHttpService implements tower_service::Service<http::Request<RequestBody>>, so an outer Tower/Axum middleware layer can run before rmcp's service consumes the request.
The exact release documentation says the service consumes the body but injects the remaining http::request::Parts into rmcp Extensions, accessible through RequestContext.
The same exact source explicitly documents that custom Axum/Tower extension state is available inside Parts.extensions and shows RequestContext -> Parts -> typed AppState lookup.
The stateless direct-dispatch path inserts the http::request::Parts into the MCP request extensions before serving the request.

source_qualified_composition.pattern: Place trusted authentication middleware outside StreamableHttpService. The middleware validates client credentials, mints a server-authenticated Principal, inserts that Principal into http::Request::extensions_mut(), and only then calls the inner rmcp service. Tool/task handlers recover http::request::Parts from RequestContext extensions, recover Principal from Parts.extensions, and fail closed before any task-store lookup or mutation if Principal is absent or invalid.
source_qualified_composition.trust_boundary: Only the server-side authentication middleware may mint Principal. Client-controlled MCP _meta, raw HTTP headers, task_id, or request arguments are inputs to validation and must never themselves be treated as the authenticated identity.
source_qualified_composition.ownership_binding: The first application-owned task-store access remains principal-scoped, e.g. (principal_id, task_id), so merely propagating Parts does not grant task ownership.
source_qualified_composition.stock_scope_limit: rmcp provides the Tower service surface and extension propagation seam, not authentication, Principal semantics, task ownership enforcement, persistent create-or-get, restart redrive, or exactly-once external effects.

falsification_and_scope.positive_scope: Source-level composition seam only; no compile, runtime server, credential validation, or effect execution was performed.
falsification_and_scope.negative_guard: A handler that reads a raw Authorization header or client _meta directly as identity fails the trust-boundary requirement even though those values are visible through Parts/request data.
falsification_and_scope.residual_dependency_detail: Turning this source seam into an operational route still requires a resident HTTP server/auth middleware runtime outside scheduled Chat unless an already-Chat-exposed connector supplies the same authenticated-principal propagation. Therefore this finding is not Phase-1 acceptance.
falsification_and_scope.quota_note: The source mechanism itself is not tied to a monthly/trial/paid hosted quota, but an accepted Chat-native route still must avoid external hosted compute entirely.
